pairs.fullEnglish: And these are the generations of Yitzchak son of Avraham: Avraham fathered Yitzchak.
Yitzchak was forty years old when he took Rivkah, daughter of בְּתוּאֵל the Aramean from פַּדַּן אֲרָם, sister of Lavan the Aramean, as his wife.
יְיָ said to her, 'Two peoples are in your womb, and two kingdoms will separate from your womb; one kingdom will grow stronger than the other kingdom, and the elder will be subject to the younger.'
Her days for giving birth were completed, and behold, there were twins in her womb.
Yitzchak loved Esav because he ate of his game, and Rivkah loved Yaakov.
Yaakov cooked a dish, and Esav came from the field (alternate reading: came in from the field), and he was exhausted.
Esav said, 'Behold, I am going to die; what use, then, is the birthright to me?'
Yaakov gave Esav bread and a dish of lentils. He ate and drank, arose and went away; and Esav despised the birthright.
There was a famine in the land, apart from the first famine that had been in the days of Avraham. Yitzchak went to אֲבִימֶלֶךְ, king of the Philistines, to גְּרָר.
יְיָ revealed Himself to him and said, 'Do not go down to Egypt; dwell in the land that I shall tell you.'

'Reside in this land, and My Word will be your aid, and I shall bless you; for to you and to your children I shall give all these lands, and I shall establish the covenant that I swore to Avraham your father.'
'I shall make your children as numerous as the stars of heaven, and I shall give your children all these lands; and all the peoples of the earth will be blessed on account of your children.'
Yitzchak dwelt in גְּרָר.
אֲבִימֶלֶךְ called Yitzchak and said, 'But surely she is your wife! How, then, did you say, “She is my sister”?' Yitzchak said to him, 'Because I said, “Lest I die on her account.”'
אֲבִימֶלֶךְ commanded all the people, saying, 'Whoever harms this man or his wife shall certainly be put to death.'
Yitzchak sowed in that land, and in that year obtained a hundred for one in his barley; and יְיָ blessed him.
The man became great, and continued going on and growing (alternate reading: increasing and growing), until he became very great.
All the wells that his father's servants had dug in the days of Avraham his father, the Philistines stopped up and filled with earth.
אֲבִימֶלֶךְ said to Yitzchak, 'Go away from us, for you have become very much stronger than we are.'
Yitzchak went away from there, encamped in the valley of גְּרָר, and dwelt there.

Yitzchak again dug the wells of water that they had dug in the days of Avraham his father, which the Philistines had stopped up after Avraham died. He called them by names like the names by which his father had called them.
Yitzchak's servants dug in the valley and found there a well of flowing spring water.
The shepherds of גְּרָר quarreled with Yitzchak's shepherds, saying, 'The water is ours.' He called the name of the well עִסְקָא, because they contended with him.
They dug another well, and they quarreled over it too; and he called its name שִׂטְנָה.

He moved away from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. He called its name רְחֹבוֹת and said, 'For now יְיָ has made room for us, and we shall multiply in the land' (alternate reading: 'and He will make us multiply in the land').
He went up from there to בְּאֵר שָׁבַע.

יְיָ revealed Himself to him that night and said, 'I am the God of Avraham your father. Do not fear, for My Word is your aid; I shall bless you and make your children numerous on account of Avraham My servant.'
He built an altar there and prayed in the name of יְיָ; he spread his tent there, and Yitzchak's servants dug a well there.
אֲבִימֶלֶךְ went to him from גְּרָר, together with a company of his friends and פִּיכֹל, the commander of his army.
Yitzchak said to them, 'Why have you come to me, when you hated me and sent me away from you?'
They said, 'We have indeed seen that the Word of יְיָ was your aid, and we said: Let the oath that was between our fathers now be established between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you.'
He made a feast for them, and they ate and drank.
They arose early in the morning and swore to one another. Yitzchak sent them away, and they went from him in peace.
On that day Yitzchak's servants came and told him about the well that they had dug, and said to him, 'We have found water.'
He called it שִׁבְעָה; therefore the name of the city is בֵּארָא דְשֶׁבַע (alternate reading: בְּאֵר שֶׁבַע) to this day.
Esav was forty years old, and he took as a wife יְהוּדִית, daughter of בְּאֵרִי the Hittite, and בָּשְׂמָת, daughter of אֵילוֹן the Hittite.
When Yitzchak had grown old and his eyes had become too dim to see, he called Esav his elder son and said to him, 'My son.' He said to him, 'Here I am.'
He said, 'Behold, now I have grown old; I do not know the day on which I shall die.'
'And now, take now your weapons, your sword and your bow, and go out to the field and hunt game for me.'
'Prepare dishes for me as I love them, and bring them in to me, and I shall eat, so that my soul may bless you before I die.'
Rivkah heard when Yitzchak spoke to Esav his son. Esav went to the field to hunt game to bring back.
Rivkah said to Yaakov her son, saying, 'Behold, I heard your father speaking with Esav your brother, saying:'
'“Bring me game and prepare dishes for me, and I shall eat and bless you before יְיָ, before my death.”'
'And now, my son, heed me concerning what I am commanding you.'
'You shall bring them to your father (alternate reading: bring them in to your father), and he shall eat, so that he may bless you before his death.'
Yaakov said to Rivkah his mother, 'Behold, Esav my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.'

'Perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall be in his eyes like one who mocks; and I shall bring curses upon myself, and not blessings' (alternate wording: 'and I shall be bringing curses upon myself').
He went and took them and brought them to his mother, and his mother made dishes as his father loved them.
She put the skins of the young goats over his hands and over the smoothness of his neck.
She placed the dishes and the bread that she had made in the hand of Yaakov her son.
He went in to his father and said, 'Father.' He said, 'Here I am. Who are you, my son?'
Yaakov said to his father, 'I am Esav your firstborn. I have done as you spoke with me' (alternate wording: 'as you told me'). 'Arise now, recline and eat of my game, so that your soul may bless me.'
Yitzchak said to his son, 'How is it that you were so quick to find it, my son?' He said, 'Because יְיָ your God made it ready before me.'
Yitzchak said to Yaakov, 'Come near now, so that I may feel you, my son: are you indeed my son Esav, or not?'
Yaakov came near to Yitzchak his father, and he felt him and said, 'The voice is Yaakov's voice, but the hands are Esav's hands.'
He did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like the hands of Esav his brother (alternate wording: covered with hair); and he blessed him.
He said, 'Are you indeed my son Esav?' He said, 'Here I am.'

He said, 'Bring it near before me, and I shall eat of my son's game, so that my soul may bless you.' He brought it near to him, and he ate; and he brought him wine (alternate reading: brought wine in to him), and he drank.
Yitzchak his father said to him, 'Come near now and kiss me, my son' (alternate wording: 'and give me a kiss').
'May יְיָ give you of the dew of heaven and of the goodness of the earth, and an abundance of grain and wine' (alternate form: 'an abundance').

'May peoples serve you, and kingdoms become subject to you. Be master over your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed, and may those who bless you be blessed.'

When Yitzchak had finished blessing Yaakov, and Yaakov had only just gone out from the presence of Yitzchak his father, Esav his brother came from his hunting (alternate reading: came in from his hunting).
He too prepared dishes and brought them in to his father, and said to his father, 'Let my father arise and eat of his son's game, so that your soul may bless me.'
Yitzchak his father said to him, 'Who are you?' He said, 'I am your son, your firstborn, Esav.'

Yitzchak was exceedingly astonished with a great astonishment, and said, 'Who, then, was that one who hunted game and brought it in to me? I ate of it all before you came in, and I blessed him; indeed, blessed he shall be.'
When Esav heard his father's words, he cried a very great and bitter cry, and said to his father, 'Bless me, me too, Father' (alternate wording: 'Bless me also, Father').
He said, 'Your brother came in with wisdom and received your blessing.'

Yitzchak answered and said to Esav, 'Behold, I have made him a master for you' (alternate reading: 'over you'), 'and all his brothers I have given him as servants; I have sustained him with grain and wine. Here, then, what shall I do for you, my son?'
Esav said to his father, 'Have you only one blessing, Father? Bless me, me too, Father.' Esav raised his voice and wept.
'By your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother. And it shall be, when his children transgress the words of the Torah, that you shall remove his yoke from upon your neck.'
The words of Esav her elder son were reported to Rivkah. She sent and called Yaakov her younger son and said to him, 'Behold, Esav your brother is lying in wait for you, to kill you.'
'And now, my son, heed me; arise and go to Lavan my brother, to חָרָן.'
'Stay with him a few days, until your brother's anger subsides.'
'Until your brother's anger toward you subsides, and he forgets what you have done to him; then I shall send and bring you from there. Why should I be bereaved of both of you in one day?'

Rivkah said to Yitzchak, 'I am distressed with my life because of the Hittite daughters. If Yaakov takes a wife from the Hittite daughters, like these, from the daughters of the land, what use is life to me?'
Yitzchak called Yaakov and blessed him, and commanded him and said to him, 'Do not take a wife from the daughters of כְּנָעַן.'
'Arise, go to פַּדַּן אֲרָם, to the house of בְּתוּאֵל, your mother's father, and take yourself a wife from there, from the daughters of Lavan, your mother's brother.'
'May אֵל שַׁדַּי bless you, make you fruitful and make you numerous, and may you become an assembly of tribes.'
'May He give you the blessing of Avraham, to you and to your children with you, so that you may inherit the land of your sojourning, which יְיָ gave to Avraham.'
Yitzchak sent Yaakov away, and he went to פַּדַּן אֲרָם, to Lavan son of בְּתוּאֵל the Aramean, brother of Rivkah, the mother of Yaakov and Esav.

Esav saw that Yitzchak had blessed Yaakov and sent him to פַּדַּן אֲרָם to take himself a wife from there; when he blessed him, he commanded him, saying, 'Do not take a wife from the daughters of כְּנָעַן.'
Yaakov heeded his father and his mother, and went to פַּדַּן אֲרָם.
Esav saw that the daughters of כְּנָעַן were displeasing in the eyes of Yitzchak his father.
Esav went to Yishmael and took מַחֲלַת, daughter of Yishmael son of Avraham, sister of נְבָיוֹת, as his wife in addition to his wives.
Yitzchak prayed before יְיָ on behalf of his wife, because she was barren; יְיָ accepted his prayer, and Rivkah his wife conceived.

qualifications.he: 'בעבור אשתו' מוסר את הקשר שבין התפילה לעקרותה. לָקֳבֵל יכול גם לציין יחס של 'כנגד/מול'; הנוסח אינו קובע היכן עמדו בני הזוג ואינו שולל גוון מרחבי.
qualifications.en: 'On behalf of his wife' conveys the prayer's relation to her barrenness. לָקֳבֵל can also express 'opposite/in relation to'; this wording neither locates the couple physically nor excludes a spatial nuance.

pairs.fullEnglish: The children pressed against one another in her womb, and she said, 'If so, why am I thus?' She went to seek instruction from before יְיָ.

qualifications.he: השאלה המקוצרת נשמרת 'למה אני כך'. המשפט אינו מפרש את ההשלמה החסרה, ולכן אין כאן קביעה שרבקה שאלה למה ביקשה היריון או למה היא חיה.
qualifications.en: The compressed question remains 'why am I thus?' The clause does not supply the missing complement; it is not expanded to 'why did I seek pregnancy?' or 'why am I alive?'.

pairs.fullEnglish: Afterward his brother came out, his hand grasping Esav's heel, and he called his name Yaakov. Yitzchak was sixty years old when she bore them.

qualifications.he: הפועל וּקְרָא הוא ביחיד. זהות הקורא אינה נקובה במשפט; 'הוא קרא' משמר זאת ואינו מכריע שהקורא הוא יצחק או מחליף את היחיד ברבים.
qualifications.en: וּקְרָא is singular. Its subject is not expressly named in this clause; 'he called' preserves that limitation without identifying Yitzchak or replacing the singular with a plural.

pairs.fullEnglish: The boys grew up. Esav was a man skilled in hunting, a man who went out to the field; Yaakov was a wholehearted man, serving in the house of instruction.

qualifications.he: המונח נַחְשִׁירְכָן נמסר בתחום הציד. 'מיומן בציד' אינו קובע דרגת מומחיות מסוימת ואינו מוסיף טענה על רמאות או על עיסוק אחר.
qualifications.en: נַחְשִׁירְכָן is rendered in its hunting sense. 'Skilled in hunting' does not specify a professional rank or add deceit or another occupation.

qualifications.he: 'משמש בבית הלימוד' משמר הן את לשון השירות והן את מקום הלימוד. המקור אינו מפרט תפקיד מוסדי מסוים, ואין להחליף את בית הלימוד באוהלים כלליים.
qualifications.en: 'Serving in the house of instruction' preserves both the service language and the place of learning. The source does not specify a particular institutional office; it is not reduced to generic tents.

pairs.fullEnglish: Esav said to Yaakov, 'Let me taste now some of this red, red stuff, for I am exhausted.' Therefore he called his name אֱדוֹם.

qualifications.he: אֱדוֹם נשמר בצורת המקור. קְרָא הוא פועל ביחיד, אך המשפט אינו נוקב בשם הקורא; אין כאן קביעה שהקורא הוא יעקב או עשו, ואין להפוך את הפועל לרבים.
qualifications.en: אֱדוֹם is retained in its source form. קְרָא is singular but the clause does not name its subject; the translation does not identify Yaakov or Esav as the namer or pluralize the verb.

pairs.fullEnglish: Yaakov said, 'Sell me your birthright this very day.'

qualifications.he: הביטוי, מילולית 'כיום הזה', נמסר 'ביום הזה ממש'. ייתכן בו גם גוון של ודאות; הנוסח אינו קובע מנגנון משפטי נפרד של תחילת תוקף ואינו מתרגם ודאות כעובדה מוכרעת.
qualifications.en: The expression, literally 'as this day', is rendered 'this very day'. It may also carry an emphasis on certainty. The wording neither adds a separate legal effective-date mechanism nor treats that possible emphasis as settled.

pairs.fullEnglish: Yaakov said, 'Swear to me this very day.' He swore to him and sold his birthright to Yaakov.

qualifications.he: כמו בפסוק 31, 'ביום הזה ממש' משמר את זיקת הביטוי ליום הזה. גוון אפשרי של ודאות נשאר מסויג; אין כאן הוספת תנאי משפטי או שינוי העובדה שעשו נשבע ומכר.
qualifications.en: As in verse 31, 'this very day' retains the expression's reference to the present day. A possible emphasis on certainty remains qualified; no legal condition is added, and the actual oath and sale are unchanged.

pairs.fullEnglish: 'Because Avraham heeded My Word and kept the charge of My Word, My commandments, My statutes, and My teachings.'

qualifications.he: קְיָמַי נמסר 'חוקותי' בתוך רשימת הציוויים. זהו תרגום לפי ההקשר; אין בכך קביעה שכל שימוש באותה משפחת מילים פירושו חוק, או שהפריט הזה זהה לברית שבפסוק 3.
qualifications.en: קְיָמַי is rendered 'My statutes' in the command list. This is a contextual equivalent, not a claim that every occurrence of the word family means a statute or that this item is identical to the covenant in verse 3.

pairs.fullEnglish: When his days there had become many, אֲבִימֶלֶךְ, king of the Philistines, looked out through the window and saw, and behold, Yitzchak was laughing with Rivkah his wife.

qualifications.he: 'צוחק עם' משמר את לשון הצחוק. ההקשר עשוי לכלול שעשוע או משחק אינטימי, והוא שמביא לבירור הנישואין בפסוק הבא; לא נקבעה פעולה גופנית מסוימת ולא נוספה המילה 'בחיבה' כאילו נאמרה במקור.
qualifications.en: 'Laughing with' retains the laughter language. The context can include playful or intimate interaction and leads to the recognition of marriage in the next verse; no specific physical act or explicit adjective 'affectionate' is asserted.

pairs.fullEnglish: אֲבִימֶלֶךְ said, 'What is this that you have done to us? The distinguished one among the people might very nearly have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.'

qualifications.he: זהו 'המיוחד בעם', לא סתם 'אחד העם'. ההקשר עשוי לרמוז לשליט, אך המשפט אינו נוקב בשמו כמבצע; הנוסח שומר את הכינוי בלי לקבוע זהות נוספת.
qualifications.en: The expression denotes 'the distinguished one among the people', not merely 'one of the people'. The context may point to the ruler, but this clause does not name him as the actor; the designation is preserved without supplying that identity.

pairs.fullEnglish: 'That you will do us no harm, just as we have not harmed you, and just as we have done you only good and sent you away in peace. You are now blessed by יְיָ.'

qualifications.he: מילולית 'אם תעשה עמנו רעה', בהמשך לשבועה שבפסוק 28. באנגלית נמסר תוכן ההתחייבות המבוקשת: שלא יעשה להם רעה. התוצאה או העונש אינם מפורשים בנוסחת השבועה, והטענה שלא הזיקו לו היא טענת הדוברים.
qualifications.en: Literally 'if you do evil to us', continuing the oath in verse 28. English expresses the requested undertaking not to harm them. The oath formula leaves its consequence or penalty unspoken, and the claim not to have harmed him is the speakers' own claim.

pairs.fullEnglish: They were disobedient and provoking toward the word of Yitzchak and Rivkah.

qualifications.he: נשמרים סירוב והתנהגות מרגיזה ביחס לדבר יצחק ורבקה. הגוון המדויק של מְרַגְּזָן — הכעסה או תגובה כעוסה — אינו מוכרע בניסוח הרחב; אין לראות בו קביעה מפורשת מי כועס, ואין לצמצמו לצער סתמי.
qualifications.en: Refusal and provocative conduct in relation to the word of Yitzchak and Rivkah are retained. The broad wording does not settle whether מְרַגְּזָן emphasizes causing anger or an angry response; it does not explicitly assign the experiencer of anger and must not be reduced to generic grief.

pairs.fullEnglish: 'Go now to the flock and take for me from there two good young goats, and I shall make them into dishes for your father, as he loves them.'

qualifications.he: הביטוי נמסר 'שני גדיים טובים'. בַר מופיע בסוגריים במקור ומבטא יחס של בן/צאצא; אין הוא מוסיף בעל חיים שלישי. מעמד הסוגריים וההתאמה הדקדוקית אינם מוכרעים כאן, אך משמעות שני גדיי העזים אינה משתנה.
qualifications.en: The phrase is rendered 'two good young goats'. The parenthetical בַר expresses an offspring relationship, not a third animal. The status of the parentheses and the grammatical agreement are not adjudicated here; they do not change the two young goats conveyed in English.

pairs.fullEnglish: His mother said to him, 'It was said concerning me in prophecy that the curses will not come upon you, my son. Only heed me, and go and take them for me.'

qualifications.he: עֲלַי נמסר כאן 'בנוגע אלי', בשימור היחס 'עלי' ובלי להחליפו ב'אלי'. המשפט אינו מפרט את אופן מסירת הנבואה או את נמענה. הקביעה המפורשת היא שלא יבואו הקללות על הבן; אין זו קבלת קללה על האם.
qualifications.en: עֲלַי is rendered 'concerning me', retaining 'upon/concerning me' rather than substituting an explicit 'to me'. The clause does not specify how the prophecy was delivered or its addressee. Its express assurance is that the curses will not come upon the son; it is not the mother's acceptance of a curse upon herself.

pairs.fullEnglish: Rivkah took the clean garments of Esav her elder son that were with her in the house, and clothed Yaakov her younger son.

qualifications.he: 'נקיים' משמר את לשון הארמית. המשפט אינו מפרט אם מדובר בניקיון רגיל או בטהרה במובן מסוים; אין כאן קביעה של מעמד הלכתי, ואין להחליף אוטומטית ב'חמודות'.
qualifications.en: 'Clean' retains the Aramaic wording. The clause does not specify ordinary cleanliness versus a particular purity sense; no legal purity status is asserted, and 'choice' is not automatically substituted.

pairs.fullEnglish: He said, 'Rightly he called his name Yaakov, for he has outwitted me these two times: he took my birthright, and behold, now he has received my blessing.' He said, 'Have you not left a blessing for me?'

qualifications.he: הפועל קְרָא נשמר ביחיד בלי לקבוע מי קרא בשם. עשו קושר את השם לכך שאחיו החכים עליו; לא נוספה אטימולוגיה שאינה כתובה בארמית, והטענה נשארת בפי עשו.
qualifications.en: The singular קְרָא is retained without identifying the namer. Esav links the name with his brother's outwitting him; no etymology absent from the Aramaic is added, and the claim remains Esav's speech.

pairs.fullEnglish: Yitzchak his father answered and said to him, 'Behold, your dwelling shall be from the goodness of the earth and from the dew of heaven above.'

qualifications.he: 'מן הטוב' נשמר כאן באופן מילולי. הניסוח אינו מכריע בין מקור/השתתפות בטוב ובין ריחוק ממנו; אין לקרוא אותו כהכרעה ב'הרחק מטוב הארץ' או כהבטחת שפע חיובית מוכרעת. אותה זהירות חלה על 'ומטל' בהמשך המשפט.
qualifications.en: 'From the goodness' is retained literally. This does not decide between source/participation and separation; it must not be read as an established 'away from the goodness' or as a separately settled positive grant of abundance. The same caution applies to 'and from the dew' in the following phrase.

pairs.fullEnglish: Esav harbored enmity toward Yaakov because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him. Esav said in his heart, 'The days of mourning for my father will draw near, and I shall kill Yaakov my brother.'

qualifications.he: הפועל נמסר כעתיד: 'יקרבו ימי אבל אבי'. בדיבור הפנימי עשוי להישמע גם גוון של משאלה; אין כאן קביעה של תאריך מוות או תוספת שעשו מתכוון להרוג את אביו.
qualifications.en: The verb is rendered as future: 'The days of mourning for my father will draw near.' The internal speech may also carry a wish-like force; no death date or intention to kill his father is added.

pairs.fullEnglish: He had flocks, herds of cattle, and a great deal of labor (alternate wording: much service); and the Philistines envied him.

qualifications.he: לשון העבודה והשירות נשמרת בלי לזהותה בהכרח עם קבוצת אנשים. היא עשויה לכלול את עבודת המשק ואת העוסקים בה; המקור כאן אינו מפרט את מספרם, את מעמדם או סוג נכסים נוסף.
qualifications.en: The labor/service language is retained without necessarily identifying it with a body of people. It can include the work of the establishment and those performing it; this clause does not specify their number, status, or an additional property class.

pairs.fullEnglish: The burden of the word of יְיָ concerning Israel, through Malachi, whose name is called Ezra the scribe.
I have loved you, says יְיָ. And if you say, ‘In what way have You loved us?’—was not Esau a brother to Jacob? says יְיָ; yet I loved Jacob.
But Esau I kept far away, and I made his mountains a desolation and his inheritance a wilderness wasteland.

For the Edomites will say, ‘We became poor; now we have become rich. We shall return and rebuild the ruins.’ Thus says יְיָ צְבָאוֹת: They will build, but I will demolish. They will be called ‘the territory of the wicked people’ and ‘the people upon whom He brought a curse forever.’

Look: a son is commanded to honor his father, and a servant to fear before his master. If I am like a father, where is the honor you show before Me? And if I am like a master, where is your fear before Me? says יְיָ צְבָאוֹת to you, priests who despise My name. And if you say, ‘In what way have we despised Your name?’—
I almost came to be amid every kind of evil, within the congregation and assembly.
Drink water from your own cistern, and flowing water from your own well.
Let your springs pour forth outside, and streams of water in the broad places.
Let them be yours alone, and let strangers have no share with you.
May your fountain be blessed, and rejoice in the wife of your youth.
You bring a rejected offering upon My altar. And if you say, ‘In what way is it rejected?’—in that you say, ‘The table of יְיָ is contemptible.’

And when you bring a blind animal to sacrifice, is that not evil? And when you bring a lame or sick animal, is that not evil? Offer it now to the governor who rules over you: will he be pleased with you, or show you favor? says יְיָ צְבָאוֹת.
And now, pray, then, before God, that He may accept our prayer. This has come about through your hands; will favor be shown to you? says יְיָ צְבָאוֹת.

Who, even here among you, will shut the doors of My Sanctuary, so that you do not bring a rejected offering upon My altar? There is no pleasure before Me in you, says יְיָ צְבָאוֹת, and I will not accept an offering from your hands with favor.
For a man’s ways are before the eyes of God, and all his paths are revealed before Him.
The wicked man’s iniquities seize him, and he will be bound in the cords of his sins.
He will die without discipline, and in the abundance of his foolishness he will go astray.

For from the rising of the sun to its setting My name is great among the nations. And whenever you do My will, I will accept your prayer; My great name is sanctified through you, and your prayer is like a pure offering before Me. For My name is great among the nations, says יְיָ צְבָאוֹת.
But you profane it by saying, ‘The table of יְיָ is contemptible, and the gifts from it are contemptible.’

Cursed is the one who acts deceitfully: he has a male animal in his flock and is bound by a vow, but sacrifices a damaged animal before יְיָ. For I am a great King, says יְיָ צְבָאוֹת, and My name is mighty among the nations.
And now, this command is for you, priests.
My son, if you have become a guarantor for your companion, if you have pledged your hand to a stranger,
you have been ensnared by the utterance of your mouth; you have been caught by the utterance of your mouth.
Do not give sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids,
so that you may escape like a gazelle from a snare and like a bird from a trap.

If you do not accept this, and if you do not lay fear of Me upon your heart, to give honor to My name, says יְיָ צְבָאוֹת, I will send the curse among you and curse your blessing. Indeed, I have cursed it, because you do not lay fear of Me upon your heart.
You will know that I have sent this command to you so that My covenant with Levi may endure, says יְיָ צְבָאוֹת.
The Torah of truth was in his mouth, and falsehood was not found on his lips. In peace, willingness, and uprightness he walked before Me, and he turned many back from sin.
For a priest’s lips should guard knowledge, and instruction should be sought from his mouth, because he serves before יְיָ צְבָאוֹת.
Turn to the ant, lazy one; observe their ways and become wise.
She prepares her bread in summer and gathers her food at harvest.
How long—until when—will you sleep, lazy one? And when will you rise from your sleep?
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of your hands to sleep,
and your poverty will come striding, and your want like a capable man.
But you have turned aside from the way; you have caused many to stumble in the Torah. You have corrupted the covenant with Levi, says יְיָ צְבָאוֹת.
So I, too, have made you contemptible and weak before all the people, because you do not keep the ways that are right before Me and you show partiality in the Torah.
Do we not all have one father? Did not one God create us? Why, then, should each of us act falsely toward his brother, nullifying the covenant with our fathers?
May יְיָ cut off from the towns of Jacob the son and grandson of the man who does this. And if he is a priest, may he have no one who offers an offering in the Sanctuary of יְיָ צְבָאוֹת.
An oppressive person, an unjust man, goes about with crooked speech in his mouth.
He is devious in his heart and forges evil at every time; he sows quarrels.
Therefore his ruin will come suddenly; suddenly he will be broken, and there will be no healing for him.
There are six things that God hates, and at seven His soul feels revulsion.
Your eyes will see, and you will say, ‘May the glory of יְיָ increase; He has enlarged the territory of Israel.’

qualifications.he: יִסְגֵי מובא כאן כלשון משאלה לריבוי כבוד ה׳. וְאַפְתֵּי נשמר כפעולה שהושלמה: הוא הרחיב את גבול ישראל, ולא כמשאלה נוספת שירחיבו. אין כאן קביעה של היקף הגבול או של מועד ההרחבה, ואין להחליף את הרחבת הגבול בלשון על כבוד שמחוץ לו.
qualifications.en: יִסְגֵי is rendered here as an acclamation wishing for increased Divine glory. וְאַפְתֵּי is retained as a completed action: He has enlarged Israel's territory, not a further wish that He may enlarge it. Neither the extent nor the date of that enlargement is specified, and enlargement of the territory is not replaced by greatness beyond it.
qualifications.anchor: יִסְגֵי יְקָרָא דַייָ וְאַפְתֵּי יַת תְּחוּם יִשְׂרָאֵל

pairs.fullEnglish: Look: I am rebuking you through the yield of sown grain. I will expose the shame of your sins upon your faces, put an end to the splendor of your festivals, and your portion will be withheld from it.

qualifications.he: רְבוּת מתורגמת כאן ׳תפארת׳, במובן גדולתם של החגים, בלי לקבוע שמדובר בכמות של תבואה, קרבנות או רכוש. מִנֵיהּ נשמר כ׳ממנו׳; אין בתרגום זיהוי מפורש נוסף של הדבר שממנו יימנע החלק. נוסח זה אינו כולל את דימויי הפרש והנשיאה שבמקרא.
qualifications.en: רְבוּת is rendered here as 'splendor,' expressing the festivals' greatness without specifying a quantity of grain, offerings, or property. מִנֵיהּ remains 'from it'; no further explicit identity is supplied for that from which the portion is withheld. This wording does not contain the biblical imagery of dung and being carried away.
qualifications.anchor: וַאֲבַטֵל רְבוּת חַגֵיכוֹן וְיִתְמְנַע חוּלָקְכוֹן מִנֵיהּ

pairs.fullEnglish: And why, my son, should you go astray with a foreign woman? Also, do not embrace the bosom of another woman (variant reading: ‘the love of another woman’).

qualifications.he: הקריאה הראשית עוּבָא היא ׳חיק׳; הקריאה החלופית המסופקת חוּבָא מובאת כאן כ׳אהבה׳ בהקשר של חיבוק ואישה אחרת. אלה שתי קריאות נפרדות, לא שני מושאים מצטברים של הציווי. אין לתקן את אותיות המקור או למזג את החלופה בקריאה הראשית.
qualifications.en: The main reading עוּבָא is 'bosom'; the supplied alternative חוּבָא is rendered here as 'love' in the context of embracing and another woman. These are separate readings, not two cumulative objects of the prohibition. The source letters are not corrected and the alternative is not merged into the main reading.

pairs.fullEnglish: Those of the house of Judah have acted falsely, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and Jerusalem. For those of the house of Judah have profaned their own soul, which had been holy before יְיָ, who loved it, and they have chosen to take for themselves wives who are daughters of worshippers of the stars.

qualifications.he: נַפְשֵׁהוֹן נשמרת כלשון ׳נפשם׳: נפש ביחיד השייכת לרבים, כמתואר גם בדַהֲוָת קַדִישָׁא. דִרְחַם נקשרת כאן אל ה׳, הנושא הזכרי היחיד המפורש הסמוך, והנפש מובנת כמושא האהבה מן ההקשר; כינוי מושא נפרד אינו כתוב במילה דִרְחַם. אין כאן החלפה של הנפש במקום קדוש או שינוי של בנות עובדי הכוכבים ל׳בת אל נכר׳.
qualifications.en: נַפְשֵׁהוֹן is retained as 'their own soul': a singular soul belonging to plural possessors, also described by the feminine singular דַהֲוָת קַדִישָׁא. דִרְחַם is linked here to יְיָ, the adjacent explicit masculine singular subject; the soul is understood from context as the object of love, not expressed by a separate object suffix in דִרְחַם. The soul is not replaced with a holy place, nor the daughters of star-worshippers with 'a daughter of a foreign god.'
qualifications.anchor: נַפְשֵׁהוֹן דַהֲוָת קַדִישָׁא קֳדָם יְיָ דִרְחַם

pairs.fullEnglish: And if you say, ‘Look at what we have brought from our weary labor,’ and you have tormented it, says יְיָ צְבָאוֹת; you bring what has been taken by force, and what is lame and sick, and you bring it as an offering. Shall I accept it with favor from your hands? says יְיָ.

qualifications.he: ׳מיגיעתנו המעייפת׳ משמר את תחום היגיעה והלאות של מִלֵאוּתָנָא, בלי לקבוע באיזה עמל מדובר. וְשַׁנֵיקְתּוּן יָתֵיהּ נשמר כ׳ועיניתם אותו׳; הכינוי ׳אותו׳ אינו מוחלף בשם של מושא שאינו מפורש במשפט. הקישור נשמר כו׳ החיבור, בלי לקבוע יחס סיבתי בין האמירות ובלי להמיר את העינוי בלשון נפיחה.
qualifications.en: 'From our weary labor' preserves the toil/weariness scope of מִלֵאוּתָנָא without specifying what work was done. וְשַׁנֵיקְתּוּן יָתֵיהּ remains 'and you have tormented it'; 'it' is not replaced by a named object that the clause does not explicitly supply. Plain coordination does not impose a causal relationship between the statements or substitute snuffing for tormenting.

pairs.fullEnglish: My covenant with him was life and peace, and I gave him complete instruction in My Torah; he feared My name.

qualifications.he: שְׁלִים הוא תואר בזכר יחיד ומתייחס אל אוּלְפָן, ׳לימוד׳, לאחר הצירוף ׳לימוד תורתי׳. אין הוא תואר של התורה עצמה, שהיא נקבה. לאחר צירוף זה שְׁמִי הוא מושא היראה, והוּא מציין את הירא: ׳את שמי הוא ירא׳.
qualifications.en: שְׁלִים is masculine singular and qualifies אוּלְפָן, 'instruction', after the phrase 'instruction in My Torah'. It does not describe the Torah itself, whose noun is feminine. In the following clause שְׁמִי is the object of fear and הוּא identifies the one who feared: 'My name he feared.'
qualifications.anchor: וְיַהֲבַת לֵיהּ אוּלְפָן אוֹרַיְתִי שְׁלִים שְׁמִי דְחִיל הוּא

pairs.fullEnglish: The first came out red, all of him like a cloak of hair (alternate reading: like a mantle of hair), and they called his name Esav.

qualifications.he: שני הנוסחים מדמים את מראה השיער לבגד עוטף: גְלִים נמסר כגלימה, וכְלָן כאדרת או מעטה. באנגלית נבחרו cloak ו־mantle כמונחים כלליים; אין הם קובעים גזרה שונה של הבגד או את חומרו. דִּשְׂעָר שייך לדימוי בשני הנוסחים. דברי רש״י על טלית של צמר מסבירים את העברית, ואינם קביעה שהמילה הארמית החלופית פירושה בגד צמר.
qualifications.en: Both readings compare the hairy appearance to an enveloping garment: גְלִים is rendered cloak and כְלָן mantle. These are broad English garment terms, not claims about different tailoring or material. The hair description applies in both readings. Rashi's woollen-garment explanation concerns the Hebrew and does not establish wool as the lexical meaning of the alternate Aramaic noun.

pairs.fullEnglish: The men of the place asked about his wife (alternate wording: concerning the matter of his wife), and he said, 'She is my sister,' because he was afraid to say, 'My wife,' lest the men of the place kill him on account of Rivkah, for she was beautiful in appearance.

qualifications.he: לְאִתְּתֵיהּ נקרא כאן כנושא השאלה, ׳על אשתו׳, ולא כפנייה לאישה שתשיב. הדבר מתאים להמשך וַאֲמַר ולכינויי אֲחָתִי ואִתְּתִי שבפי האיש המשיב. החלופה עַל עֵיסַק אִתְּתֵיהּ אומרת במפורש ׳על עניין אשתו׳; היא נשמרת כחלופה ואינה מחליפה את אותיות הנוסח הראשי. פירוש רש״י ל׳לאשתו׳ שבמקרא, ׳עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ׳, מסייע להשוואת התחביר, אך אינו מובא כעדות נפרדת למילה ארמית אחרת. ההריגה נמסרת כחשש בלבד.
qualifications.en: לְאִתְּתֵיהּ is read here as the topic of the inquiry, ‘about his wife,’ not as an address requiring the woman to answer. This fits the following masculine וַאֲמַר and the answering man's ‘my sister’ and ‘my wife.’ The alternate עַל עֵיסַק אִתְּתֵיהּ expressly says ‘concerning the matter of his wife’; it remains an alternate and does not replace the main source letters. Rashi's explanation of the Biblical Hebrew לאשתו as עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ supports the syntactic comparison, but is not presented as separate evidence for a different Aramaic word. Killing is expressed only as a feared possibility.

pairs.fullEnglish: It has no harvest, just as it has neither an overseer nor a ruler.

qualifications.he: חַצְדָא מתורגם כאן ׳קציר׳, כשם הדבר, ולא ׳קוצר׳ או ׳קצין׳. הֵיךְ אַף לָא משווה בין שלילות: אין לה קציר, כשם שאין לה גם ממונה ושליט. הצירוף הבלתי רגיל של הקציר עם בעלי התפקידים נשמר; אין מוסיפים הסבר כיצד היא משיגה את מזונה או הופכים את הקציר לבעל תפקיד.
qualifications.en: חַצְדָא is rendered here as the noun 'harvest,' not 'reaper' or 'chief.' הֵיךְ אַף לָא compares negative statements: it has no harvest, just as it also has neither an overseer nor a ruler. The unusual juxtaposition of harvest and officeholders is retained; no account of how it obtains its food is added, and the harvest is not turned into an officeholder.
qualifications.anchor: דְלֵית לָהּ חַצְדָא הֵיךְ אַף לָא סָרְכָא וְשַׁלִיטָא

pairs.fullEnglish: He signals with his eyes, stamps with his feet, and gestures with his fingers.

qualifications.he: תָכֵס הוא פועל של כתישה או רקיעה, וכאן הרגליים הן כלי הפעולה. מילון יאסטרוב מביא את השורש תכס במשמעות זו ומציין במפורש את הפסוק הזה; הערך המילוני מנוקד תְּכַס, ואילו בפסוק זה הצורה היא תָכֵס. התי״ו היא חלק מן השורש, ולא תחילית המציינת נמען בגוף שני. הצורה הפעילה ביחיד ממשיכה את תיאורו של אותו אדם המרמז בעיניו ובאצבעותיו. אין כאן פירוט של עוצמת הרקיעה, מקצבה או קוד האיתות שלה. פירוש השפשוף של הרגליים שנאמר על מוֹלֵל שבפסוק העברי אינו משמש תחליף לפועל הארמי, ואין תוספת של הסתה לעבודה זרה.
qualifications.en: תָכֵס is a verb of crushing or stamping, here performed with the feet. Jastrow gives this meaning under the consonantal root תכס and expressly cites this verse; the dictionary headword is pointed תְּכַס, whereas this passage has תָכֵס. The initial ת belongs to the root, rather than marking a second-person addressee. The active singular form continues the description of the same man who signals with his eyes and fingers. The force, rhythm and particular signaling code of the stamping are not specified. The explanation of foot rubbing given for מוֹלֵל in the Hebrew verse is not substituted for the Aramaic verb, and incitement to idolatry is not added.

pairs.fullEnglish: Do this, my son, and escape, because you have fallen into your companion’s hand: go, stir up your companion now.

qualifications.he: גְרֵג מורה כאן על הנעה או זירוז של החבר, ולא על בקשה נמרצת בפני עצמה. חֲבִיל נקראת כמילת קישור או זמן, ׳עתה׳: במילון היא נזכרת במפורש ככתיב שבדפוסים של פסוק זה לצד היכיל, הכיל והביל, בהוראת ׳לכן, עתה׳. חֲבִיל אינה כאן פועל נוסף המצווה לפגוע בחבר או לכבול אותו. חַבְרָךְ הוא המושא של גְרֵג. התיאור קורא להיחלצות מן המצב שבו נפל הבן לידי חברו, אך אינו מפרט דרך מעשית, תשלום, הבאת מתווכים או היתר להטריד או להזיק.
qualifications.en: גְרֵג here means to stir up or rouse the companion, rather than an independently established act of pleading earnestly. חֲבִיל is read as the connective or temporal particle 'now': the dictionary expressly records it as a printed spelling at this verse alongside היכיל, הכיל and הביל, under 'therefore, now.' חֲבִיל here is not a second verb commanding injury or binding. חַבְרָךְ is the object of גְרֵג. The passage calls for escape from the situation in which the son has fallen into his companion's hand, but specifies no practical method, payment, recruitment of intermediaries, or permission to harass or harm.

pairs.fullEnglish: A doe of love and a gazelle of grace—learn kindness at every time, and study continually in her love.

qualifications.he: ״צבי של חן״ הוא תיאור רחב של דמות בעל החיים דִיצְתָּא, ולא זיהוי של מין זואולוגי מודרני. תַדְוָנָא מתפרשת כאן כשם עצם במשמעות חסד או נדיבות, המוקדם לפועל הציווי אֲלַף: למד חסד. אין במילה סיומת כינוי שמשמעה ״שדיה״, ואין כאן מילת יחס שמשמעה ״מן״. הכינוי הנקבי מפורש דווקא בוּבְרַחֲמוּתָהּ — באהבתה. אֲלַף ותִּגְרַס מביעים לימוד ועיסוק חוזר בלימוד, ובְּכָל זְמַן ותְּדִירָא מציינים את התמשכותם. לשונות אלה עוסקות בלימוד, בניגוד ללשונות הרוויה והשגייה שבפסוק העברי. במילון נזכרת גם קריאת מהדורת לגארד הֲוָונָא; אין היא הקריאה תַדְוָנָא שבנוסח זה.
qualifications.en: 'A gazelle of grace' is a broad rendering of the animal image דִיצְתָּא, not an identification of a modern zoological species. תַדְוָנָא is understood here as a noun meaning kindness or liberality, placed before the learning imperative אֲלַף: learn kindness. The word does not contain a possessive ending meaning 'her breasts,' and no preposition meaning 'from' appears here. The feminine reference is explicit instead in וּבְרַחֲמוּתָהּ, 'in her love.' אֲלַף and תִּגְרַס express learning and repeated study, while בְּכָל זְמַן and תְּדִירָא give their continuing temporal scope. These Aramaic predicates speak of learning and repeated study, rather than the Hebrew verse's satisfaction and infatuation. The dictionary also records Lagarde's reading הֲוָונָא; that is not the reading תַדְוָנָא in this text.
qualifications.anchor: וְדִיצְתָּא דְחֶסְדָא תַדְוָנָא אֲלַף בְּכָל זְמַן וּבְרַחֲמוּתָהּ תִּגְרַס תְּדִירָא

explanation.he: יצחק מתפלל לפני יְיָ בעבור רבקה, וקבלת תפילתו נזכרת במפורש. רבקה מבקשת הוראה לנוכח הדוחק שבבטנה. התשובה מתארת שני עמים ושתי מלכויות, ואת שעבוד הגדול לקטן.
explanation.en: Yitzchak prays before יְיָ concerning Rivkah, and the acceptance of his prayer is explicit. Rivkah seeks instruction because of the pressing within her womb. The answer describes two peoples and two kingdoms, with the elder becoming subject to the younger.

dayTitle.en: The Brothers' Birth and Their Different Ways

explanation.he: לידת עשו מתוארת באמצעות צבעו ושיערו, ואחריו נולד יעקב כשידו אוחזת בעקב אחיו. בהמשך התרגום מעמיד את איש הציד היוצא לשדה מול האיש השלם המשמש בבית הלימוד. אהבת יצחק לעשו נקשרת במפורש באכילה מצידו, ואהבת רבקה ליעקב נזכרת בנפרד.
explanation.en: Esav's birth is described through his redness and hair, and Yaakov follows with his hand grasping his brother's heel. The translation then contrasts the hunter who goes out to the field with the wholehearted man serving in the house of instruction. Yitzchak's love for Esav is expressly connected with eating his game, while Rivkah's love for Yaakov is stated separately.

dayTitle.en: The Dish, the Birthright, and the Oath

explanation.he: עשו מבקש לטעום מן התבשיל האדום ומנמק את בקשתו בעייפותו. יעקב מבקש את מכירת הבכורה ולאחר מכן שבועה, והתרגום מזכיר במפורש גם את השבועה וגם את המכירה. דברי עשו על מותו נשמרים כדבריו, בלי לקבוע כאן מה מקור הסכנה שהוא רואה.
explanation.en: Esav asks to taste the red dish and gives his exhaustion as the reason. Yaakov requests the sale of the birthright and then an oath; both the oath and the sale are explicit. Esav's statement about dying remains his own statement, without an added explanation of the danger he perceives.

dayTitle.en: The Despised Birthright and the Renewed Covenant

explanation.he: לאחר האכילה והשתייה נאמר שעשו ביזה את הבכורה. הרעב מביא את יצחק לגרר, ושם הוא מצטווה שלא לרדת למצרים. ההבטחה מנוסחת כסיוע של המימר, ברכה, נתינת הארצות וריבוי הבנים, ונקשרת לשמירת אברהם את דברי הציווי.
explanation.en: After the eating and drinking, Esav is said to have despised the birthright. Famine brings Yitzchak to גְּרָר, where he is told not to descend to Egypt. The promise includes the aid of the Word, blessing, the gift of the lands, and numerous children, and is connected to Avraham's observance of the commands.

dayTitle.en: The Sister Claim and the Discovery of the Marriage

explanation.he: יצחק מציג את רבקה כאחותו מתוך פחד שיהרגוהו בגללה. המראה הנשקף מן החלון מביא את אבימלך לקרוא לו ולברר את דבריו. אבימלך מתאר את סכנת האשמה שהייתה עלולה לבוא על הציבור עקב שכיבה עם אשת איש.
explanation.en: Yitzchak presents Rivkah as his sister because he fears being killed on her account. What is seen through the window leads אֲבִימֶלֶךְ to summon him and question his statement. The king describes the guilt that could have come upon the people through intercourse with a married woman.

dayTitle.en: Blessing, Wells, and an Oath of Peace

explanation.he: היבול הרב וריבוי המקנה מלווים בקנאת הפלשתים וביציאה מגרר. יצחק שב לחפור את בארות אביו, וממשיך לחפור גם לאחר מריבות על המים. דבר ההבטחה חוזר ומזכיר את סיוע המימר, ואבימלך וחבריו מבקשים לקיים שבועה שהייתה בין האבות. בסיום נזכרים נישואי עשו, יחס נשותיו לדברי יצחק ורבקה, וקריאת יצחק הזקן לבנו הגדול.
explanation.en: The abundant crop and livestock are accompanied by Philistine envy and departure from גְּרָר. Yitzchak reopens his father's wells and continues digging after disputes over the water. The renewed promise again names the aid of the Word, and אֲבִימֶלֶךְ and his companions seek to establish the oath that existed between their fathers. The reading ends with Esav's marriages, his wives' response to the words of Yitzchak and Rivkah, and the aged Yitzchak's summons to his elder son.

dayTitle.en: The Blessings, Esav's Threat, and Yaakov's Departure

explanation.he: רבקה מדריכה את יעקב ומזכירה אמירה בנבואה שלפיה לא יבואו עליו הקללות. יצחק בוחן את הקול ואת הידיים, אוכל ומברך, ולאחר שוב עשו מאשר שהמבורך יישאר ברוך. בדברי יצחק לעשו תלויה הסרת העול בכך שבני אחיו יעברו על דברי התורה. איום עשו מביא להוראת רבקה ללכת ללבן, ולאחר מכן יצחק שולח את יעקב עם ציווי בענייני נישואין ועם ברכת אברהם. בסיום עשו מבחין ביחס אביו לבנות כנען ונושא את מחלת בת ישמעאל נוסף על נשותיו.
explanation.en: Rivkah directs Yaakov and invokes a prophetic declaration that the curses will not come upon him. Yitzchak examines the voice and hands, eats and blesses, and after Esav returns affirms that the one blessed will remain blessed. In Yitzchak's words to Esav, removal of the yoke is conditioned on his brother's children transgressing the words of the Torah. Esav's threat leads Rivkah to direct Yaakov to Lavan, after which Yitzchak sends him with a command concerning marriage and the blessing of Avraham. At the end, Esav recognizes his father's attitude toward the daughters of כְּנָעַן and marries מַחֲלַת, daughter of Yishmael, in addition to his wives.

dayTitle.en: Love for Jacob and Honor for the Divine Name

explanation.he: התרגום מזהה את מלאכי כעזרא הסופר, ומתאר את אהבת ה׳ ליעקב לעומת הרחקת עשו וחורבן נחלתו. אדום מבקש לשוב ולבנות, אך בניינו עתיד להיהרס. בסיום מופנית אל הכוהנים שאלת הכבוד והיראה, בדימויי בן ואב ועבד ואדון.
explanation.en: The Targum identifies Malachi as Ezra the scribe and describes Divine love for Jacob in contrast to Esau’s rejection and the devastation of his inheritance. Edom intends to rebuild, but its building will be demolished. The reading closes by challenging the priests about honor and fear through the relationships of son and father, and servant and master.

dayTitle.en: Revealed Paths and the Bonds of Sin

explanation.he: הקריאה מזהירה את הבן שלא לסטות אל אישה נוכרייה ואל חיקה של אחרת. היא מדגישה שכל דרכי האדם גלויות לפני האלוהים. העוונות מתוארים כאוחזים ברשע, והחטאים כחבלים הכובלים אותו בדרכו חסרת המוסר.
explanation.en: The reading warns the son against straying with a foreign woman and embracing another woman’s bosom. It emphasizes that all a person’s ways are revealed before God. Iniquities seize the wicked man, while sins become cords binding him as he wanders without discipline.

dayTitle.he: תפילה כקרבן טהור ושמירת כבוד השם
dayTitle.en: Prayer as a Pure Offering and Honor for the Name

explanation.he: התרגום מתאר תפילה המתקבלת כאשר ישראל עושים את רצון ה׳: שמו הגדול מתקדש על ידם, ותפילתם נחשבת כקרבן טהור לפניו. כנגד זאת ניצבים ביזוי השולחן והמתנות והבאת קרבן שנלקח בכוח או שיש בו פגם. הקריאה מזהירה גם מפני רמייה בקיום נדר, וחותמת בהפניית הציווי אל הכוהנים.
explanation.en: The Targum describes prayer accepted when Israel does the Divine will: His great name is sanctified through them, and their prayer is like a pure offering before Him. This is contrasted with contempt for the table and its gifts, and with offerings taken by force or bearing defects. The reading also condemns deceit in fulfilling a vow and closes by directing the command to the priests.

dayTitle.en: From Entrapping Words to Urgent Escape

explanation.he: הקריאה פונה לבן שנעשה ערב לחברו ומסר את ידו לנוכרי. דברי פיו מתוארים כמלכודת שבה נתפס, והפנייה לחבר מוצגת כדחופה. ההימנעות משינה ודימויי הצבי והציפור מבטאים את הצורך להיחלץ מן הלכידה.
explanation.en: The reading addresses a son who has become a guarantor for his companion and pledged his hand to a stranger. His own words are described as a trap that has caught him, and approaching his companion is presented as urgent. The refusal of sleep and the images of a gazelle and a bird express the urgency of escaping that entrapment.

dayTitle.en: The Covenant with Levi and the Torah of Truth

explanation.he: הקריאה מזהירה מפני קללה וביטול הברכה כאשר אין מניחים את יראת ה׳ על הלב ואין נותנים כבוד לשמו. מנגד עומדת ברית החיים והשלום עם לוי, הקשורה בלימוד התורה וביראת השם. תורת אמת, שפתיים נקיות משקר והליכה בשלום וברצון מתארות את מי שמשיב רבים מן החטא ומשרת לפני ה׳.
explanation.en: The reading warns of a curse and the undoing of blessing when fear of God is not laid upon the heart and honor is not given to His name. In contrast stands the covenant of life and peace with Levi, joined to Torah instruction and fear of the Divine name. True Torah, lips free of falsehood, and walking in peace and willingness describe one who turns many from sin and serves before יְיָ.

dayTitle.en: The Ant’s Ways and the Lazy Person’s Delay

explanation.he: העצל נקרא להתבונן בדרכי הנמלה וללמוד מהכנת מזונה בקיץ ומאיסופו בקציר. שאלות על אורך השינה מציבות כנגד עבודתה את הדחייה החוזרת של הקימה. המעט המצטבר של שינה, תנומה וחיבוק ידיים מוביל לתיאור בואם של העוני והמחסור.
explanation.en: The lazy person is called to observe the ant’s ways and learn from her preparation of food in summer and gathering at harvest. Questions about the length of sleep contrast her work with repeated delay in rising. The accumulating little periods of sleep, slumber, and folded hands lead to a description of poverty and want arriving.

dayTitle.en: Corrupting the Covenant and Betraying Brotherhood

explanation.he: הקריאה מוכיחה את הכוהנים על סטייה מן הדרך, הכשלת רבים ונשיאת פנים בתורה. שאלות על האב האחד ועל האל האחד שברא את כולם מציבות מול הבגידה את האחווה ואת ברית האבות. בהמשך מתואר חילול נפשם של אנשי יהודה בבחירת נשים מבנות עובדי הכוכבים, והאזהרה מפרטת בן ובן בן ותנאי מיוחד למי שהוא כוהן.
explanation.en: The reading rebukes the priests for turning aside, causing many to stumble, and showing partiality in Torah. Questions about one father and the one God who created everyone set brotherhood and the ancestral covenant against their false dealing. It then describes the profaning of Judah’s own soul by choosing wives from the daughters of star-worshippers; the warning specifies son and grandson and a distinct condition if the offender is a priest.

dayTitle.en: Crooked Speech and the Sowing of Quarrels

explanation.he: הקריאה מתארת אדם עושק ועוול, שפיו מעוות ותנועות עיניו, רגליו ואצבעותיו מצטרפות להתנהגותו. בליבו הוא מתהפך, חורש רעה ומטיל מריבות. כנגד מעשים אלה מתואר שבר פתאומי, והסיום פותח את מניין ששת הדברים והשבעה השנואים והמאוסים לפני האלוהים.
explanation.en: The reading portrays an oppressive and unjust person whose crooked speech is accompanied by movements of his eyes, feet, and fingers. He is devious in his heart, forges evil, and sows quarrels. Sudden ruin is set against this conduct, and the ending introduces the count of six things and seven that God hates and finds abhorrent.

dayTitle.en: The Waters of One’s Home and Love for the Wife of Youth

explanation.he: לאחר תיאור הקרבה לרעה בתוך הקהל, הקריאה עוברת למי הבור, הבאר והמעיין השייכים לאדם. דימויי המים נקשרים לברכת המקור ולשמחה באשת הנעורים, בלי שיתוף זרים. הסיום מצרף לדימויי האהבה לשונות של לימוד והתמדה.
explanation.en: After describing how close the speaker came to evil within the assembly, the reading turns to the waters of one's own cistern, well, and springs. The water imagery is joined to a blessed fountain and joy in the wife of one's youth, without strangers sharing in them. The ending joins its imagery of love to language of learning and continual study.

dayTitle.en: A Rejected Offering and the Question of Acceptance

explanation.he: הכוהנים ננזפים על הבאת קרבנות שאינם ראויים ועל אמירתם ששולחן ה׳ בזוי. התרגום משווה את הבאת הבהמה העיוורת, החיגרת או החולה למתנה שלא תתקבל גם אצל מושל בשר ודם. הקריאה מסיימת בקריאה להתפלל לקבלת התפילה ובדחיית הקרבן המובא מתוך יחס זה.
explanation.en: The priests are confronted over unacceptable offerings and their claim that the table of יְיָ is contemptible. The Targum compares bringing a blind, lame, or sick animal with presenting a gift that would not please even a human governor. The reading concludes with a call to pray for the acceptance of prayer and with rejection of an offering brought in this manner.
